items.title: Password reset does not invalidate existing sessions (stolen JWT survives 7 days)
items.notes: Stateless 7-day JWT; resetPassword() never watermarks. A stolen session/JWT keeps full dashboard+API access after the victim resets. Fix: add User.sessionsValidAfter/passwordChangedAt (schema migration), stamp on reset, embed iat at login, reject stale tokens in resolveBusinessRole/withV1Auth; add log-out-everywhere. OWASP ASVS 3.3. || ENV NOTE (Jul 9): requires a Prisma migration (sessionsValidAfter) on the dev schema; the dev DB is currently UNREACHABLE from this environment (P1001), so the migration + cross-credential-path integration test cannot be run here. Needs the dev DB reachable (or a local Postgres) to execute safely.
items.resolution: FIXED on loop/engine-bootstrap. Server-side session invalidation via a stable token.loginAt watermark (set once at sign-in, exposed as session.loginAt) compared against a new User.sessionsValidAfter column (stamped on password reset + a new logOutEverywhere() action). Enforced in resolveBusinessRole for every SESSION caller — getBusinessContext (all server actions), withV1Auth session-cookie path (all REST v1), and the dashboard layout (all RSC read pages). API keys/OAuth exempt (L-047); fail-closed on legacy tokens once a watermark is set; rollout-safe. Migration applied + verified on the rebuilt clean dev DB (watermark round-trips exactly; pre-reset session DENIED, post-reset ALLOWED, with cleanup). Caught + fixed a self-introduced flaw pre-commit (fail-closed would have killed API keys — added the opts!==undefined session-caller gate). 685/685 tests (+16). 2-lens adversarial pass: regression=fix-is-sound; completeness surfaced a PRE-EXISTING gap (internal /api/* bare-auth routes) → L-048.

items.title: Login + password-reset leak account existence via response-timing side channel
items.notes: authorize() returns before bcrypt.compare for a non-existent email; requestPasswordReset awaits sendEmail only for real emails. Fix: dummy bcrypt on the no-user branch; fire-and-forget sendEmail in reset. Lower priority than L-037 (the explicit register oracle dominates).
items.resolution: FIXED on loop/engine-bootstrap. Closed the login + password-reset timing side-channel: (1) authorize() now runs a dummy bcrypt.compare against a lazily-computed hash on the no-user / no-passwordHash branch, so a non-existent account takes the same time as a wrong password; (2) requestPasswordReset now fire-and-forgets the email send (void sendEmail(...).catch(...)) instead of awaiting it only on the user-exists branch. Test: tests/auth-timing-enumeration.test.ts (fire-and-forget proven by a never-resolving email mock that would hang the old code; + source-guard for the login closure). Gate: tsc clean, 15/15 invariants, 669/669.

items.title: authorize() never checks user.status -> a suspended user can still mint a session
items.notes: resolveBusinessRole blocks suspended users on getBusinessContext surfaces, but the 4 onboarding.ts actions authorize by ownerId only, so a suspended owner can still log in + edit business config. Fix: add 'if (user.status !== active) return null' in authorize(); optionally route onboarding through getBusinessContext. (status set out-of-band today -> P3.)
items.resolution: FIXED on loop/engine-bootstrap. authorize() in src/lib/auth.ts now refuses a non-active account AFTER a correct password check (if (!isActiveStatus(user.status)) return null), so a suspended/deactivated owner can no longer mint a session and reach the ownerId-only onboarding actions. Introduced a shared pure predicate isActiveStatus(status) in src/lib/permissions.ts (no Prisma -> no auth/auth-utils circular import) and DRY-refactored resolveBusinessRole to use it, so the login path and the live-role path can never disagree. Placed after password validation to avoid leaking suspension via timing to a wrong-password guesser. Tests: tests/is-active-status.test.ts (predicate active->true, suspended/inactive/null/undefined/unknown->false, + source-guard that auth.ts wires it); resolveBusinessRole suspended->null already covered by membership-revocation.test.ts (still green after refactor). Gate: tsc clean, 15/15 invariants, 658/658.

items.title: Account deletion revokes no credentials (session/API-key/OAuth-token/PII residue) for beta salons

Fix: in the deletion tx revoke apiKey/oAuthAccessToken (revokedAt), set user.status non-active/deletedAt, queue PII anonymization.
items.resolution: FIXED on loop/engine-bootstrap: requestAccountDeletion() now revokes the tenant's ApiKey + OAuthAccessToken (revokedAt=now) INSIDE the deletion tx, so a leaked/previously-issued API key or OAuth access token stops authenticating immediately. businessId-scoped (no cross-tenant blast radius); global User.role/status deliberately left alone (a shared member must not be logged out everywhere). Session-JWT watermark + PII anonymization tracked separately (L-034 covers session invalidation). Test: tests/account-deletion.test.ts +2 cases (revokes both tables in-tx with businessId+revokedAt:null scope; revokes nothing when authz fails).

items.title: Residual: create-payment-intent guard checks COMPLETED only — two PENDING PaymentIntents can still coexist across hours
items.notes: The L-017 guard blocks re-charging an appointment whose payment already COMPLETED. It does NOT block a second PaymentIntent while an earlier one is still PENDING (different hour bucket -> new idempotency key). Narrow race (client would have to complete two different clientSecrets), and a strict pending-guard risks permanently blocking legit re-payment when an abandoned PI leaves a stale 'pending' row that no webhook ever resolves. Proper fix needs pending-intent reuse (return the existing PI's clientSecret) + stale-pending expiry, or moving to a single canonical PaymentIntent per appointment. LATENT while Connect online payments are off; fix before go-live alongside L-001.

items.title: Admin-only READ routes (/reports, /reports/payday, /staff list) enforce role-LEVEL only via stale-JWT middleware — demoted admin reads revenue/payroll/commission/PII for up to 7 days
items.notes: Distinct from L-036: these pages have NO page-level role gate — they gate role-LEVEL only through middleware STAFF_BLOCKED_ROUTES, which reads req.auth.user.role = the 7-day JWT (auth.config.ts maxAge 7d; token.role set at login, never refreshed). layout's resolveBusinessRole only redirects on NULL membership (removed/suspended), never enforces the admin LEVEL these routes require. So a demoted admin's JWT still says 'admin' -> middleware passes -> layout resolveBusinessRole returns non-null 'staff' -> no redirect -> data renders. Surfaces: reports/page.tsx:33-66 (shop revenue + per-barber commission, P1); reports/payday/page.tsx:34-52 (payroll statements, P1); staff/page.tsx:8-16 -> getStaff selects commissionRate+email+phone (P2). Queries (getStaffPerformance/getRevenueByDay/getPayrollStatement/getStaff) enforce businessId only, no role. FIX (defense-in-depth, its own iteration): either (a) layout maps route->minRole and enforces it via the live resolveBusinessRole, or (b) convert each admin-only page to resolveBusinessRole AND push role checks down into the sensitive queries. Architectural completion of L-036.
items.resolution: FIXED on loop/engine-bootstrap. Added a LIVE-role admin gate at the top of the 3 exposed admin-only pages — reports/page.tsx, reports/payday/page.tsx, staff/page.tsx: `const liveRole = await resolveBusinessRole(userId, businessId); if (!hasRole(liveRole, 'admin')) redirect('/dashboard')` — placed BEFORE any sensitive fetch. Even when the stale-JWT middleware lets a demoted admin through, the page re-checks the current DB role and bounces them. Locked by tests/reports-staff-admin-gate.test.ts (behavioural: hasRole admin-predicate staff/null denied, admin/owner allowed; + source-guard: each page wires the live-role redirect). 2-lens adversarial workflow (wdk0eh3e4): correctness = fix-is-sound (legit admin/owner pass; gate precedes every fetch; no redirect loop; null fail-closed; redirect not swallowed). Completeness DISPROVED total coverage → 2 more sibling leaks of the SAME data class logged as L-044 (P2) + L-045 (P3). Gate: tsc clean, 15/15 invariants, 640/640.

items.title: Memoize resolveBusinessRole per-request (React cache()) — layout + page each re-resolve the role (~6 role queries/nav)
items.notes: layout.tsx calls resolveBusinessRole (3 parallel queries) on every dashboard route, and dashboard/calendar/staff[id]/clients[id]/settings each call it again on the same request. Correctness is fine (verifier: fix-is-sound) — only added latency. Wrap resolveBusinessRole in React cache() so it resolves once per request. Low risk, low priority. || ASSESSED + DECLINED (Jul 9 self-paced run): react.cache is undefined in this React 18.3.1 + vitest environment (it is only exposed under the RSC 'react-server' export condition, not the node/CJS context). Wrapping resolveBusinessRole in cache() would break every test that imports @/lib/auth-utils, or require a fragile bundler-interop-dependent guard (cache ?? identity) on the single most security-critical function — disproportionate risk for a P3 perf gain. REVISIT after a React 19 / Next upgrade (stable cache), or memoize per-request via a bundler-safe approach (e.g. an explicit request-scoped store) rather than react.cache.

items.title: Sensitive queries return pay/revenue fields to non-admins by default → commissionRate leaks via /calendar + /services, todayRevenue leaks via /api/sidebar-data
items.notes: ROOT CAUSE (the recurring sibling-leak pattern): src/lib/queries/reports.ts + payroll.ts + staff.ts enforce businessId ONLY, never role — so every caller must remember to gate, and two forgot. (1) getStaff() (staff.ts:70) returns `commission: Number(s.commissionRate)` for every staffer with no role param; /calendar (calendar/page.tsx:36→CalendarClient) and /services (services/page.tsx:19→ServicesClient) forward the full array to the client, and BOTH are staff-accessible (minRole staff, not in STAFF_BLOCKED_ROUTES) → a staff/demoted-admin reads every barber's commission from the RSC flight payload. (2) /api/sidebar-data (route.ts:60) returns dashboardStats.todayRevenue with NO role check; sidebar.tsx:342 renders it for all roles → staff GETs shop revenue. FIX (defense-in-depth root fix that closes both + any future caller): make getStaff / getStaffPerformance / getRevenueBy* / getPayrollStatement accept the caller role and STRIP pay/revenue fields (or refuse) for non-admins; and add a role check to /api/sidebar-data before returning todayRevenue. This SUPERSEDES per-caller whack-a-mole. Verified queries currently role-blind (info finding).
items.resolution: FIXED on loop/engine-bootstrap. Root-cause data-layer fix: getStaff(businessId, viewerRole?) now strips commission→0 + email→'' + phone→'' unless hasRole(viewerRole,'admin') (secure by default); only the admin-gated /staff roster passes its live role to opt back in, so the staff-accessible callers (search, /calendar, /services, /booking) can no longer leak pay/PII by default. /api/sidebar-data now gates todayRevenue on the live admin role (mirrors the dashboard page). 2-lens adversarial workflow (wadvd1aa8): regression lens = fix-is-sound (all 5 getStaff callers audited — only staff/client.tsx renders email/phone/commission and it always gets admin data; no crash on ''; no type break; sidebar revenue correct for admins, 0 for staff). Completeness lens confirmed the pay/revenue CORE fully covered across all non-MCP surfaces; the one residual is contact-PII only → logged L-046. Tests: tests/queries-staff-pii-strip.test.ts (5) + tests/sidebar-data-revenue-gate.test.ts (4). Gate: tsc clean, 15/15 invariants, 649/649.

items.title: MCP list-staff / get-staff-member return commissionRate + full user row (incl passwordHash) with no admin gate — LATENT (MCP disabled)
items.notes: src/lib/mcp/tools/staff.ts:16 list-staff does prisma.staff.findMany with no `select` (returns commissionRate/hourlyRate/employmentType/employeeId/hireDate), and get-staff-member uses `include:{user:true}` returning the full User row INCLUDING passwordHash — neither calls isAdmin(). Via OAuth withV1Auth resolves the granting user's real role, so a staff-role MCP caller would receive all colleagues' pay + PII + passwordHash. NOT currently reachable: src/app/api/mcp/route.ts hard-404s unless MCP_ENABLED==='true' (tool layer intentionally off until hardened). Close before MCP ships: add `select` (drop passwordHash + pay for non-admins) + isAdmin() gate. Mirror the REST /api/v1/staff field-stripping.

items.title: REST GET /api/v1/staff + /staff/[id] return colleague email+phone to non-admin callers (pay already stripped) — inconsistent with getStaff's PII model
items.notes: GET /api/v1/staff (route.ts:35) has no admin gate on the caller and its non-admin sanitize strips ONLY pay (commissionRate/hourlyRate/employmentType/employeeId/hireDate), leaving user.email + user.phone (selected at :25) in the response; GET /api/v1/staff/[id] has the identical gap. A staff-role session cookie or staff-scoped API key can enumerate every colleague's email+phone. The pay/revenue concern is already covered — this is contact-PII only. It CONTRADICTS L-044's dashboard model, where getStaff now strips email/phone for non-admins. MILD PRODUCT JUDGMENT (flagged, not guessed): decide whether staff may see colleague contact info. RECOMMENDED default (consistent + least-privilege): strip email/phone for non-admin callers in both v1 handlers, mirroring the pay strip already there. Note API keys default to role=admin, so blast radius is only staff-scoped keys/sessions. Low-risk one-surface fix once the policy is confirmed.
items.resolution: FIXED on loop/engine-bootstrap. GET /api/v1/staff + /api/v1/staff/[id] now strip user.email + user.phone for non-admin callers (in addition to the pay fields they already stripped), via an explicit public-user allowlist {id,firstName,lastName,avatarUrl,role} — consistent with getStaff (L-044). Adversarial completeness sweep of the whole v1 surface: v1/team GET is already admin-gated (FORBIDDEN for non-admins, so its email select is fine); v1/appointments exposes only staff firstName/lastName (no contact) and already scopes staff to their own rows; no other staff-contact-PII leak. Applied the SECURE DEFAULT (strip) rather than waiting on a policy call — API keys default to role=admin so blast radius is only staff-scoped keys/sessions; Anas can opt staff back in later if desired. Test: tests/v1-staff-pii-strip.test.ts (4: list+detail × staff/admin). Gate: tsc clean, 15/15 invariants, 653/653.

items.title: API-key Bearer path does not re-validate the key creator's live status/membership — a suspended or removed user keeps API/MCP access via an un-revoked key
items.notes: withV1Auth's Bearer API-key branch returns {userId:apiKey.createdById, businessId:apiKey.businessId, role:apiKey.role} WITHOUT calling resolveBusinessRole, so unlike the OAuth path (:76) and the session path (:94) it never checks whether the key creator is still an ACTIVE member. A suspended user (or one removed from the business) keeps full REST + MCP access through any un-revoked, un-expired API key they created. Same class as L-039, different credential surface. NUANCE: do NOT just swap in resolveBusinessRole(createdById) — an API key intentionally carries its OWN configured role (apiKey.role), which may differ from the creator's role (e.g. an admin mints a read-only key); overriding it would break the key-role model. CORRECT FIX: additionally look up the creator's status (and optionally live membership) and refuse the key when the creator is non-active, WITHOUT changing the key's configured role. Also weigh whether a key should die when its creator loses membership vs only on explicit revoke (L-040 covers deletion). Its own careful iteration.
items.resolution: FIXED on loop/engine-bootstrap. The withV1Auth Bearer API-key branch (src/lib/api/auth.ts) now calls resolveBusinessRole(apiKey.createdById, apiKey.businessId) as a LIVENESS GATE and returns null if it's null — so a suspended/deactivated or removed creator's un-revoked key stops working, mirroring the OAuth + session paths. Crucially it still returns the key's OWN configured role (apiKey.role), NOT the resolved role, preserving the key-role model (an admin can still mint a read-only key). lastUsedAt is only bumped on a successful (accepted) use. Adversarial sweep: MCP reuses withV1Auth (covered); api-keys.ts hashing is key CREATION (owner-gated); the v1/api-keys/[id] route looks up by id for management (behind withV1Auth) — no other request-auth key path exists. Test: tests/v1-apikey-creator-status.test.ts (suspended creator → key rejected + no lastUsedAt bump; active creator → accepted with the KEY's staff role even though the creator resolves admin). Gate: tsc clean, 15/15 invariants, 660/660.

items.title: Rate limiter is in-memory (module-level map) — ineffective across serverless instances; not applied to all ~38 mutating v1 routes
items.notes: BLOCKED on an OWNER decision + enabler: needs a shared store (Upstash Redis via env var, fall back to in-memory for local dev) to be serverless-correct. Provisioning Upstash is a cost/account decision. src/lib/rate-limit.ts. L-035's per-IP login throttle depends on this — do RL-1 BEFORE L-035. DONE when limits hold across two simulated instances + a progress.md checklist maps every v1 route to its limit.

items.title: No DB-level exclusion constraint on bookings (advisory lock only; no btree_gist EXCLUDE as defense-in-depth)
items.notes: BLOCKED here on dev-DB reachability + the btree_gist extension. Add an EXCLUDE constraint on appointments (tstzrange over staff+time) via a dev-schema migration; audit every create/reschedule path for lock coverage. DONE when a raw-SQL overlapping insert is rejected by the DB itself and all booking tests stay green. (Migration cannot be applied/tested from the current environment — DB server unreachable, P1001.)

items.title: Internal /api/* route handlers authenticate via bare auth() and skip BOTH the live-role check (L-036) and the session watermark (L-034) — stale/removed sessions read PII + initiate card charges
items.notes: These /api/* routes live OUTSIDE the (dashboard) layout and do NOT use getBusinessContext or withV1Auth, so they trust the raw 7-day JWT businessId with no live-role and no watermark: /api/stripe/create-payment-intent (P2 — FINANCIAL MUTATION: mints a Stripe PaymentIntent + Payment row; no resolveBusinessRole at all), /api/search (P2 — leaks client names+emails, services, staff), /api/notifications (P2 — leaks appointments, payment amounts, reviews), /api/sidebar-data (P2 — calls resolveBusinessRole WITHOUT opts so the watermark is silently skipped; also only gates revenue, doesn't DENY on null role), /api/stripe/dashboard-link + /api/stripe/connect (P3 — stale owner keeps Stripe account access), src/lib/actions/onboarding.ts actions (info — bare auth()+ownerId, self-tenant). CONSEQUENCE: both a DEMOTED/REMOVED member (L-036 class) and a STALE post-reset session (L-034 class) still reach these. FIX: a shared route-handler auth helper (the getBusinessContext equivalent for /api routes) that resolves the LIVE role + enforces the watermark (passes {sessionLoginAt}) and returns 401 on null; route all bare-auth() /api handlers + onboarding actions through it. High-value: closes a financial-mutation + PII bypass in one systemic change.
items.resolution: DONE @ e50848c. New shared helper src/lib/api/route-auth.ts: getRouteBusinessContext() (getBusinessContext equivalent for /api route handlers — live role + ALWAYS forwards {sessionLoginAt} so the L-034 watermark is enforced; returns null -> 401) and getLiveUserId() (pre-business variant: live status + watermark, for the onboarding actions which have no businessId in the JWT yet). Converted: /api/stripe/create-payment-intent, /api/search, /api/notifications, /api/sidebar-data (now DENIES on null role instead of only zeroing revenue), /api/stripe/connect, /api/stripe/dashboard-link, and all four src/lib/actions/onboarding.ts actions. All six routes 401 before any DB read/Stripe call/write. Adversarial verify (4 lenses): CONFIRMED-SOLID — opts can never be undefined, no loginAt laundering (auth.config stamps loginAt only on sign-in), forged/stale cross-tenant businessId resolves null, no missed session-authed siblings (billing-portal/subscription-checkout/bookings/calendar all use getBusinessContext; public routes verified public-by-design). Residuals logged as L-050/L-051/L-052. 31 new/updated tests; 708 unit green; 15/15 invariants.

items.title: Password reset + logOutEverywhere do not revoke OAuth access tokens / API keys — a 'suspected compromise' reset leaves programmatic credentials fully alive
items.notes: resetPassword (password-reset.ts) and logOutEverywhere (account.ts) stamp sessionsValidAfter (kills SESSIONS) but do NOT revoke apiKey / oAuthAccessToken — only requestAccountDeletion does (L-040). Since API keys + OAuth are watermark-exempt (L-047, correct), a compromise that triggers a reset / log-out-everywhere leaves any stolen API key or OAuth token with full programmatic access. logOutEverywhere's own doc says 'use after a suspected compromise', so leaving programmatic creds alive is a real gap. DECISION (product): should reset / log-out-everywhere also revoke the user's API keys + OAuth tokens? RECOMMENDED: logOutEverywhere revokes both (revokedAt=now) as the 'kill everything' action; password reset optionally too (or surface a prompt). Mirror the revocation already in requestAccountDeletion.

items.title: /onboarding page read path still uses bare auth() — a stale post-reset or suspended session can read the (own) business name/phone/address/hours while un-onboarded
items.notes: src/app/onboarding/page.tsx:9-27 renders business details with bare auth(), no liveness/watermark. Low impact: read-only, own-business only, and only while the business has no active services (line 34 redirects onboarded users into the watermark-checked dashboard layout). Fix: resolve the user via getLiveUserId() (src/lib/api/route-auth.ts) and redirect('/login') on null. The onboarding ACTIONS are already gated (L-048).

items.title: resolveBusinessRole's owner lookup has no deletedAt filter — the owner of a soft-deleted business still resolves a live role
items.notes: src/lib/auth-utils.ts:30 business.findFirst({id, ownerId}) lacks deletedAt: null, so a soft-deleted business's owner keeps a role and can read /api/search, /api/notifications, /api/sidebar-data (and any getBusinessContext surface) for the deleted business. Pre-existing (shared with getBusinessContext, predates L-048); the Stripe routes independently filter deletedAt. DECIDE first: is post-soft-delete owner access intended (grace period / restore window)? If not, add deletedAt: null to the owner lookup + a test.

items.title: Error-shape cleanups: denied callers get 500/200-empty instead of 401 on three surfaces
items.notes: (a) src/lib/actions/oauth.ts:23-25 'if (!ctx)' is dead code — getBusinessContext throws, so a denied caller gets an unhandled server-action error rather than {success:false}; (b) src/app/api/calendar/[appointmentId]/route.ts:101-104 unauthenticated -> 500 not 401; (c) /api/search + /api/notifications catch-alls return 200 with empty payloads, masking outages (no data leak). Denial IS enforced everywhere — these are correctness-of-shape fixes, not bypasses.
